intro: Antigua and Barbuda is a two-island nation said to have a beach for every day of the year.

chapters.title: Early peoples
text: Arawak and later Kalinago peoples lived here. Columbus named Antigua in 1493 after a church in Seville.

chapters.title: British sugar colony
text: English settlers arrived in 1632. Sugar plantations used enslaved Africans; in 1736 a planned uprising led by Prince Klaas was crushed. Nelson's Dockyard was a key Royal Navy base in the 1700s and is now a World Heritage site.

highlight.title: Nelson's Dockyard
highlight.text: Horatio Nelson was based here in the 1780s.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Antigua and Barbuda became independent in 1981. In 2017 Hurricane Irma forced the whole population of Barbuda to evacuate.

keyTerms.meaning: A place for building and repairing ships.
